deviations.what: The measurement lookups are a SQL UNION of two pk subqueries, and the geometry helpers are static methods of a Spatial class in managers.py, not public methods of each queryset.
deviations.why: An OR of two pk__in conditions scans the measurement table; the helpers are needed by the measurement queryset, whose lookup signatures differ.

deviations.what: Project.spatial_coverage counts public datasets and those the viewer holds a level on.
deviations.why: Plan D6 says 'datasets the viewer may open' without a rule; this is the one the dataset overview uses for its siblings.

deviations.what: CHANGELOG.md got added entries and the Dataset.bbox removal, outside T020's wording.
deviations.why: The spec asks for every breaking change in the changelog and the docs check names removed symbols.

concerns: fairdm/core/dataset/templates/publishing/datacite44.xml cannot be rendered in this environment: `{% load partials %}` raises KeyError for the library on the unmodified template too, and no test renders it. My edit (box read from dataset.spatial_coverage, centroid block left for US7) was not verified by a render.
`manage.py makemigrations --check` lists a pending migration for the third-party `orbit` app (orbit 0008_alter_orbitentry_type); no fairdm app has one. Not touched.

TestQueryPlan loads 6,000 rows and takes about 25 seconds; it reads the plans the natural planner picks, with ANALYZE on the sample, measurement, organization and contributor tables. A planner change on a new PostgreSQL major could flip it, which is the signal it exists to give.

The collection listing uses visible_to for a measurement's effective location, so a published but private dataset's sample places no measurement for a visitor. This is D3, but it differs from what the listing's own published() scoping shows for the sample itself.
